questions.question: Who among the following was the first Muslim woman ruler of medieval India from 1236 to 1240 AD?
questions.solution:
• Razia Sultana: Razia Sultana
  • Reign: 1236–1240. First Muslim woman ruler of medieval India.

questions.question: Who among the following began the Suddhi Movement, which enabled the Hindus who had accepted Islam or Christianity to return to Hinduism, their original faith?
questions.solution:
• Suddhi Movement: Dayanand Saraswati
  • Purpose: A ceremony to bring back converts to Hinduism.

questions.question: What was the main reason for the defeat of Sirajuddaulah at the Battle of Plassey?
questions.option_1: Britishers cut the food supplies of Sirajuddaulah forces compelling them to surrender.
questions.option_2: Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle.
questions.option_3: Sirajuddaulah's prime minister misinformed the location of Britishers.
questions.option_4: Britishers knew the secret way to enter Sirajuddaulah's palace.
questions.solution:
• Plassey Betrayal: Forces led by Mir Jafar never fought
  • Note: Mir Jafar's treachery ensured Robert Clive's victory.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of Mahajanapada Gandhara in 6th century BC?
questions.solution:
• Gandhara Capital: Taxila
  • Fact: A world-renowned center of learning on the Silk Road.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced?
questions.solution:
• Morley-Minto Viceroy: Lord Minto
  • 1909: Introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Deccan Education Society (1884)?
questions.solution:
• Deccan Education Society: G G Agarkar
  • Founders: Tilak, Agarkar, and Chiplunkar founded it in 1884.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental college?
questions.solution:
• MAO College: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
  • Evolution: Founded in 1875 at Aligarh; later became AMU.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of Buddhist stupas?
questions.solution:
• Not part of Stupa: Gopura
  • Context: Gopuras are temple gateways in Dravidian architecture.

questions.question: In 1526, Babur defeated the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, at ______ and captured Delhi and Agra.
questions.solution:
• Panipat (1526): Panipat
  • Outcome: Babur replaced the Delhi Sultanate with the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Qutub-ud-din Aibak founded which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
• Slave Dynasty: Slave Dynasty
  • Founder: Qutub-ud-din Aibak, originally a general of Ghori.

questions.question: Which British governor ended the Dual System of Government in Bengal?
questions.solution:
• End of Dual System: Warren Hastings
  • 1772: He abolished the system where the Company had power without responsibility.

questions.question: Who among the following led the Battle of Buxar on behalf of British East India Company?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Buxar Leader: Hector Munro
  • Outcome: Defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim and Shah Alam II.

questions.question: What does ‘Chaitya’ in Buddhist architecture refer to?
questions.solution:
• Chaitya: Prayer hall
  • Design: Characterized by a stupa at the end of a long vaulted hall.

questions.question: Who among the following addressed the Indian National congress as its President in 1887?
questions.solution:
• 1887 President: Badruddin Tyabji
  • Record: He was the first Muslim president of the INC.

questions.question: Which Chola ruler built the Brihadeshwara Temple at Tanjore?
questions.solution:
• Brihadeshwara Temple: Rajaraja I
  • Fact: A masterpiece of Dravidian architecture in Thanjavur.

questions.question: Buddha attained enlightenment at ______.
questions.solution:
• Bodh Gaya: Bodh Gaya
  • Enlightenment: Buddha meditated under the Pipal tree here.

questions.question: Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer came to India in ______.
questions.solution:
• Vasco da Gama (1498): 1498
  • Landing: Arrived at Calicut (Kozhikode).

questions.question: Mukteshwara Temple is a 10th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, located in __________.
questions.solution:
• Mukteshwara Temple: Odisha
  • Architecture: Located in Bhubaneswar, famous for its stone arch (Torana).

questions.question: Gautamiputra Shri Satakarni was a ruler of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Gautamiputra Satakarni: Satavahana
  • Achievement: Restored the prestige of the dynasty; the 'destroyer of Shakas'.

questions.question: Who among the following was a leader of the Khilafat Movement?
questions.solution:
• Khilafat Leader: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
  • 1919: Led the movement to protect the Ottoman Caliph.

questions.question: In which year, did Sher Khan defeat Humayun at Kanauj?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Kanauj (1540): 1540
  • Fate: Humayun was decisively defeated by Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri).

questions.question: After the Revolt of 1857 was put down by Britishers, which Mughal ruler was forced to leave the country?
questions.solution:
• Exile of 1857: Bahadur Shah Zafar
  • Destination: Deported to Rangoon (Burma) after the trial.

questions.question: Who among the following emphasised the worship of God as Nirankar (formless) in Punjab, India?
questions.solution:
• Nirankar Worship: Baba Dayal Das
  • Movement: Founded the Nirankari movement for formless worship.

questions.question: Who among the following Chahamana ruler defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori in 1191?
questions.solution:
• First Battle of Tarain: Prithviraja III
  • 1191: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Ghori.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Dantidurga: Dhantidurga
  • Origin: Founder of the Rashtrakuta Empire.
